title: The Morning Run (Chas McIvor)
style: country blues acoustic guitar warm baritone male vocal storytelling 104bpm walking bass brushed drums honest character portrait unhurried Perth ocean fishing charter
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The morning run begins at first light when the harbour's half asleep
The Pelican slips the moorings and heads out toward the deep
Pete at the wheel, the clients in their jackets at the rail
Reading the horizon for the signs that never fail

[Pre-Chorus]
My brother reads the ocean like a man who learned the language
Not from books but from being in it — that's the advantage

[Chorus]
The morning run, the morning run
Out of Fremantle harbour with the rising of the sun
The morning run, the morning run
Every trip a different ocean under the same sky's gun
Pete knows what's running and where the ledge will be
The morning run is what the free look like when they're free
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The clients want the yellowtail and Pete knows where they are
By reading the temperature, the birds, the colour of the scar
Where two water masses meet and the fish are gathered there
Pete's been past that spot a hundred times and knows to steer

[Bridge]
From the roof of any house in Perth you see the Indian Ocean flat
And something in it calls a certain kind of man and that
Is Pete — who answered what the ocean called and went
And made himself a charter skipper — and made himself content

[Outro]
Morning run knows Pete by name now… the ocean knows Pete…
That's my boy
